en.t: A useful thing to add to an AI prompt: "Ask me what you need to know before you start."
en.d: For a vague task, those questions can be more valuable than an immediate draft. Who will use this? What decision should it support? What information is missing? I'd keep it to a few questions so the conversation stays practical. What would change if your AI asked for clarification before filling in the gaps? #AI #Prompting #ProblemSolving #Communication…

en.t: Some useful AI tasks sound pretty boring.
en.d: Shortening an email. Organizing scattered notes. Finding the confusing sentence in a proposal. I like these as starting points because the task is specific and the result is easy to check. en.t: "Make it better" leaves a lot for an AI to guess.
en.d: More readable? More convincing? Short enough to read between meetings? Try adding the audience, the purpose, and one example of what you like. Even a simple instruction becomes more useful: "Explain this to a store manager who needs to decide what to do tomorrow." Sometimes writing the prompt reveals that the goal was still unclear.
